goal: A confirmed phase worker or sub-architect whose process dies mid-task (tmux pane killed, Kubernetes pod crashed) is relaunched by the daemon with --resume on its recorded session and prompted with its state-derived catch-up: at once when its stream closes and the one reconnect is refused, and at the latest on the next resync tick when Runtime.probe reports the process gone. No new state field, no LegionState version bump, no LegionDaemonApi wire change, no runtime branching in ProcessManager.
architecture: One death path with one relaunch decision. `markWorkerDead(token, locator, observed)` runs under the role's `mutateClaim` lock: re-validate the locator (`sameProcess`), drop a cached client for the dead process, clear the locator into `resumeSessionFile` (the existing retirement, now split so it does not persist on its own), decide — tree gone or lingering → nothing; queue entry held → nothing; finished bystander → nothing + log; else `launchFailures += 1`; at `MAX_LAUNCH_FAILURES` (`===`) publish `worker-died` and stop; a pending prompt with no queue entry → enqueue for the drain; else relaunch — persist once, release the lock, `promoteWorkerQueue()`, then the existing `resumeWorker` → `deliverToWorker` path (`--resume` from `resumeSessionFile`, `catchup` prompt, cap- and launch-hold-aware). Three callers name how the death was observed: `onWorkerClientClosed` (stream-closed), `reconnectWorker` (restart-reconnect), and the new resync backstop (resync-probe): `runResync` emits `{kind:"probe-worker", token}` for every located, ready-confirmed worker claim; the pump dispatches it to `ProcessManager.probeWorkerClaim`, which probes through `Runtime.probe` outside the lock and hands a dead verdict to `markWorkerDead`. The prompt-failure breaker keeps calling `markWorkerDeadLocked` and never enters the decision.
globalConstraints: No runtime branching in ProcessManager: every liveness question goes through `Runtime.probe` (via `probeLocator`), every stop through `stopProcess`; `FakeRuntime` (kubernetes-shaped locators) is the unit-test runtime, `TmuxRuntime` the live one.

No new persisted field and no `LegionState` version bump: the decision reads `launchFailures`, `pendingAssignment`, `readyConfirmedAt`, `resumeSessionFile`, `workerAdmission.queue`, `phases`, `trees` — all existing.
No `LegionDaemonApi` request/response shape change, so `LEGION_DAEMON_API_VERSION` and `packages/pi-envoy/package.json` `legion.daemonApiVersion` stay at 5.
The worker image is built only in CI; nothing in this PR builds or loads one.
`unknown` never marks anything dead; a probe that throws clears nothing; recovery is observation-based, never a hard SLA.

The relaunched worker gets the daemon's catch-up (`catchup-worker`, or `catchup-overseer` for a sub-architect), never a replay of the interrupted prompt; a queued architect `assignment` on the claim wins over the catch-up.
No new architect wake type: a relaunch publishes exactly what the existing resume path publishes; `worker-died` at the threshold is the one wake the architect acts on.

Repository conventions: Biome (double quotes, semicolons, 100 cols), `strict` tsc, Bun test, co-located `__tests__/`, `node:` imports, no barrel files. Skip formatters/linters until the final gate; run `bunx biome check packages/daemon/src`, `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun test packages/daemon` once at the end.

Commit with jj only (`jj -R "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" new` / `split`), never `abandon`/`undo`/`op restore`; push with `jj bookmark set legion/LEGION-179 && jj git push --bookmark legion/LEGION-179`; PR body must contain `Dispatch: LEGION-179`; rebase only on CONFLICTING.

Never touch the dogfood daemon, `~/.omp/profiles/legion/plugins`, `~/.config/legion/*/legion.yaml`, or a pane/pod you did not start. Live tmux rows use their own `legion-smoke<timestamp>` server; the kind proof uses a throwaway cluster you create and delete.

decisions.decision: The relaunch decision runs inside `markWorkerDead`'s `mutateClaim` callback, but the relaunch itself (`resumeWorker`) runs after the lock is released.
decisions.reason: `resumeWorker` → `deliverToWorker` acquires `mutateClaim(token)` itself and computes the catch-up with a GitHub read outside it; re-acquiring the same token's critical section from inside a callback already holding it deadlocks (see `stopProcessSerialized`'s doc comment). The decision (counter, queue check, bystander check, `worker-died`) needs the lock; the launch does not, and `deliverToWorker` re-validates the claim under its own lock (a `spawn_worker` landing in the gap wins over the catch-up).

decisions.decision: Split `markWorkerDeadLocked` into an unpersisted `retireDeadWorkerLocatorLocked` plus the existing persisting wrapper; `markWorkerDead` persists once after the decision.
decisions.reason: The locator clear and the counted failure (and, for a pending prompt, the queue push) must be one durable write — the rule `retireUnconfirmedBoot` already follows. Two saves would let a crash between them leave a locator-less, uncounted, unqueued claim that `reconnectWorkers`' locator-only filter never sees again. The breaker's `retirePromptFailedClaim` keeps the persisting wrapper unchanged.

decisions.decision: A dead confirmed claim whose `pendingAssignment` is set but whose token holds no `workerAdmission.queue` entry is enqueued for the drain (`enqueueForRetryPending`) instead of being handed a new catch-up.
decisions.reason: `deliverToWorker` drops a `catchup` when an `assignment` is pending ("the architect's assignment ... reaches the worker first") — but with no queue entry nothing would deliver it, and the worker would stall. Enqueueing is `retireUnconfirmedBoot`'s exact shape: the drain relaunches with `--resume` and delivers the pending prompt, whichever kind it is. The spec's requirement that a queued assignment wins over the catch-up is met by delivering that assignment.

decisions.decision: The tree check is `isTreeGone(treeKey, issue) || trees[treeKey].status === "lingering"`.
decisions.reason: The spec's Errors table says a worker dying while its tree is closing or lingering is not relaunched and attributes that to the existing `isTreeGone`/closing checks — but `isTreeGone` covers only `closed`, unrecorded, reparented, and `closingTrees`, not a durable `lingering` status whose worker stop failed and is waiting for the sweep. One explicit status check makes the spec's sentence true.

decisions.decision: `markWorkerDead` evicts and closes a cached client for the dead locator after the `sameProcess` check passes, before the retirement's stop.
decisions.reason: The resync path reaches a dead process whose stream never reported its close (half-open). Without eviction `stopProcess` would `awaitShutdown` on that client for the full `worker_stop_timeout_seconds` (10 s) under the role lock before killing. The stream-close path has already evicted (no-op); the restart path never connected (no-op). Eviction after the identity check never touches a newer generation's client; the evicted client's own `closed` event finds the cache moved on and returns.

decisions.decision: `probeWorkerClaim` never throws; `unknown`, a probe throw, and a `StopFailed` from the retirement are each one log line and nothing cleared.
decisions.reason: `runResync` awaits every probe with `Promise.all`; one rejected worker probe would abort the run's remaining probes and its controller payload (`resync failed:` in `index.ts`). The root `onProbe` throws through by design (one root per tree); a run probes many workers, so isolation per claim matches `reconnectWorkers`' per-claim rule.

decisions.decision: Resync emits `probe-worker` for every located, ready-confirmed worker claim regardless of its tree's status; the handler's death path applies the tree rules.
decisions.reason: `resync.ts` has no `rootForIssue`/`closingTrees`; the tree verdict (gone, closing, lingering) is `ProcessManager`'s, and applying it once in `decideWorkerRelaunch` keeps the three observation paths on one rule.

decisions.decision: The counter is `launchFailures`, `===` at the threshold, reset only by a confirmed ready — no separate crash counter.
decisions.reason: Spec acceptance 2 and Rejected; mirrors `retireUnconfirmedBoot` and `launchWorker`, so the fresh claim carries the count (`launchWorker` copies `launchFailures`), the boot watchdog adds to it if the relaunch never confirms, and `workerReady` zeroes it.

decisions.decision: The implementer's required production-like proof is two live tmux rows in `processes.test.ts` (`LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1`): a real pane killed and relaunched through the resync probe, and a real `legion worker-shim` pane killed and relaunched through the stream-close path. The kind run for acceptance 3 is planned as a host-daemon-from-this-branch + kind-pods-from-the-published-image run; whether review waits on it is the architect's call (see concerns).
decisions.reason: The repository's real-process fixtures are an accepted proof surface (legion-worker skill), they exercise the real tmux probe, kill-pane, `--resume` argv, and the real shim socket close. Acceptance 3 as written runs the in-cluster daemon from a published image, and no image can carry this branch before it merges (the Worker Image workflow's pull-request trigger fires only for `packages/daemon/docker/**`, `omp-pin.ts`, and the workflow file; post-merge it needs a `workflow_dispatch` or a release `workflow_call`). The spec itself says the fake-runtime proof stands alone until an image carries LEGION-178. The host-daemon route (`runtime.kubernetes.kubeconfig`, `daemon_url` at the kind gateway) is the runtime's own supported shape and exercises this branch's daemon against real pods now.

steps:
Insert the bullet (one paragraph, the file's style):
"- A confirmed phase worker or sub-architect whose process dies mid-task is relaunched by the daemon, not merely retired (LEGION-179). Three observations reach one death path, `markWorkerDead(token, locator, observed)`: the worker's stream closing with its one reconnect refused (`onWorkerClientClosed`, at once), the restart-time reconnect refusing (`reconnectWorker`, under the launch hold — queued, launched by `reconcileWorkerAdmission`), and the resync backstop — every `runResync` emits `{kind: "probe-worker", token}` for each worker claim with a locator and `readyConfirmedAt` (`probeConfirmedWorkers`, beside `probeActiveRoots`), dispatched to `ProcessManager.probeWorkerClaim`, which probes through `Runtime.probe` outside the role lock: `alive` is nothing; `unknown` and a probe that throws are one log line and nothing cleared (retried next tick); `dead` — `gone` or `not-recorded-process`, the latter logged with both identities — enters the death path. Under `mutateClaim(token)` it re-validates the locator with `sameProcess`, closes and drops a cached client for the dead process (a half-open stream must not hold the stop for `worker_stop_timeout_seconds`), clears the locator into `resumeSessionFile`, and decides in one persisted write: a gone, closing, or lingering tree → nothing (`closeTree`/the sweep own it); a token already on `workerAdmission.queue` → nothing (the drain relaunches it cold, once); a finished bystander (`isBystanderRole` and no `pendingAssignment`) → retired only, one log line — only `spawn_worker` resumes it; otherwise the death is one `launchFailures`, at `MAX_LAUNCH_FAILURES` (`===`) `worker-died` to the owning architect and no relaunch; a claim still holding a pending prompt is enqueued so the drain relaunches it and delivers that prompt; else, after the lock, `resumeWorker` → `deliverToWorker` resumes the same agent (`--resume` from `resumeSessionFile`, a `catchup` prompt — `catchup-worker`, or `catchup-overseer` for a sub-architect — never the interrupted task, never an `assignment`, so `phases[issue]` is untouched), cap- and hold-aware, publishing nothing new to the architect. A relaunch that confirms `/worker/ready` resets the counter as today; one that never confirms is the boot watchdog's and escalates on the same counter. Daemon-initiated stops never relaunch and need no flag: idle retirement and the prompt-failure breaker clear the locator before their stop returns, `closeTree` deletes the claim or is found in `closingTrees`, so the stop's own socket close fails the identity check or the tree check. The prompt-failure breaker's `retirePromptFailedClaim` → `markWorkerDeadLocked` keeps its own queue relaunch and never enters this decision. Every death logs one `<token>: worker process died (<how>); …` line naming how it was observed and the count."

Kill the tester's process from the node (a crash, never a graceful delete — a graceful stop lets the shim shut OMP down cleanly): `NODE=$(kind get nodes --name legion-179-proof)`; `CID=$(docker exec $NODE crictl ps -q --name worker --label io.kubernetes.pod.name=<tester pod>)`; `PID=$(docker exec $NODE crictl inspect --output go-template --template '{{.info.pid}}' $CID)`; `docker exec $NODE kill -9 $PID`. Observe in the daemon log, in order: `[legion] legion-legion179-<key>-tester: worker process died (its stream closed and the one reconnect was refused); launch failure 1/3; relaunching the same agent with --resume and its catch-up` — or, if the stream stayed half-open, within `resync_interval_seconds` the `resync-probe` variant preceded by `resync probed N active roots and M confirmed workers`; the runtime's `resuming OMP session <path>` line for the tester's generation 2; `kubectl get pod legion-<key>-tester-g2 -o jsonpath='{.spec.containers[0].args}'` carries `--resume=<the recorded session path>`; `/worker/started` accepted for generation 2 with the same session id (state's `roles[].sessionId` unchanged, `generation` 2); the catch-up delivered (the tester's turn starts — the pod's log or state's `pendingAssignment` cleared); the tester finishes: the issue moves `needs_review` and the architect receives `phase-complete` (state's `phases[<key>]` completed / the architect pod's log). Confirm no `spawn_worker` for the tester after the kill: `grep -c 'worker/spawn' <daemon log>` unchanged across the kill window.

Negative control: kill a finished worker's pod the same way (the planner's, idle after its phase, still Running before idle retirement — `worker_idle_retire_seconds` 600 gives ten minutes) → the daemon log says `… died (…) after finishing: <key>'s active phase is tester … retired, not relaunched`, no `-planner-g2` pod appears, `launchFailures` on its claim unchanged.

Record in `.legion/implement.json` `proof[]` (criterion 3): the digest, whether the LEGION-177 workaround was applied, the log excerpt, `kubectl get pods` before and after, the g2 pod's args, the status transitions, the head SHA, the negative control. Tear down: stop the daemon (SIGTERM), `kind delete cluster --name legion-179-proof`, `docker rm -f legion-179-nats legion-179-postgres`, kill the listener/Dispatch processes you started, `shred -u` the generated secrets under /tmp/legion-179.

Two small rules beyond the spec's decision list, each with its reason in `decisions`: a dead claim holding a pending prompt but no queue entry is enqueued rather than given a catch-up (otherwise `deliverToWorker` drops the catch-up behind the pending assignment and nothing delivers either); a durable `lingering` tree blocks the relaunch explicitly (`isTreeGone` does not cover it, though the spec's Errors table assumes it does).

`markWorkerDeadLocked` is split so the locator clear and the counted failure persist in one write; the breaker keeps the persisting wrapper. A reviewer may ask why not one save inside `markWorkerDeadLocked` — the answer is the breaker's different bookkeeping.

The resync run now performs one `Runtime.probe` per located confirmed worker per tick (tmux: one `list-panes` each; Kubernetes: one pod GET each). At the dogfood's scale (tens of workers, ten-minute interval) this is negligible; a deployment with hundreds of pods would want the probes batched — not this issue.
The live tmux rows need `LEGION_TMUX_LIVE=1` and a real tmux; CI does not run them, so the implementer and tester must paste their local run into the PR body.

Known limit, unchanged from today's exception path: `resumeWorker` computes the catch-up with GitHub reads (`workerCatchup` → `gh api` per PR of the issue) before `deliverToWorker`. If that read throws at the moment of death (GitHub unreachable), the claim is already retired and counted with `resumeSessionFile` kept, the throw is logged by the observing path (`clientFor`'s close-handler catch, `reconnectWorkers`' per-claim catch, `probeWorkerClaim`'s catch), and — having no locator — the claim is invisible to the next resync probe; the next role-lane exception, durable 404, or `spawn_worker` resumes it. Closing this needs `workerCatchup` to degrade to an empty `unhandled` list on a fetch failure (a catch-up semantics change: it would silently omit comments) or a retry queue for pending catch-ups; both are beyond this spec. The architect may want a follow-up issue.
